articles.title: 24 小时为你在线打工：Anthropic 推出 Claude Duet AI 智能体，迎战 Meta 和 OpenAI
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，Anthropic 昨日（10 月 21 日）宣布以研究预览版形式，推出全新应用 Claude Duet，定位为可主动工作的 AI 智能体（agent），加入由 Meta 的 Muse、以及 OpenAI 的 Dots 领衔的“全天候主动型 AI 助理”大战。技能方面，该应用会每天整理跨应用的重要事项、主动提醒需要处理的问题，并在用户离开后继续在后台完成被委托的任务。IT之家附上演示视频如下：Claude Duet 基于 Claude Opus 5.5 构建，提供 iOS、Android 独立应用及 claude.ai 网页版。首批面向美国 Pro 和 Max 订阅用户开放候补名单；预览阶段与 Claude 其他功能共享套餐用量限制。不同于普通聊天机器人，Claude Duet 拥有独立虚拟机和浏览器，可在用户设备关闭时持续运行。用户可用文字或语音下达任务，例如安排会议、整理未读邮件、追踪发票、制作财务或销售预测、搭建仪表盘、开发网页应用等；任务完成后，它会通知用户或请求审核。在工具生态方面，Claude Duet 可调用 Claude Marketplace 中超过 6,000 个连接器和插件，覆盖 Gmail、Slack、QuickBooks、Stripe、Gusto、LinkedIn、HubSpot、Canva、Shopify、DocuSign 等常见办公与商业服务。它还能通过 Link 或 Shop Pay 完成经用户确认的线上支付，并使用虚拟卡避免泄露真实卡号。安全设计方面，Anthropic 表示，Claude Duet 不会直接接触用户密码或登录 tokens；发送消息、付款、签署文件或删除内容前，必须获得用户批准。系统还配备专门分类器，拦截信用卡号、政府身份证件等高敏感信息的泄露请求。不过，Anthropic 也坦承这仍是早期版本：Claude Duet 可能误读对话、误判事项紧急程度；个人事务处理能力相对较弱，且暂不能向用户展示其浏览器操作过程。

articles.title: Meta Boosts Bet on AI With Spending Outlook, New Stock Class
articles.content: Meta Platforms boosted its capital spending outlook and announced plans for a new class of nonvoting stock, escalating its already-stratospheric bet on artificial intelligence. Capital expenditures will be $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026, the social-media giant said during its quarterly earnings report Wednesday, raising the bottom end of the range from $130 billion. The new class of shares, meanwhile, will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend. Holders will get one share of the new stock in what will essentially be a two-for-one stock split, Meta said. It expects trading of the new shares to begin in January. Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，IBM今日发布 2026 财年（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 12 月）半年报（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）及第三财季（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）报告： 2026 财年半年报 营业总收入：501.82 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3357.84 亿元人民币），同比增长 4.88% 毛利润：285.71 亿美元（现汇率约合 1911.78 亿元人民币），同比增长 4.39% 毛利率：56.9%，同比下降 0.3 个百分点 归母净利润：55.71 亿美元（现汇率约合 372.77 亿元人民币），同比增长 11.58% 经营现金流：117.91 亿美元（现汇率约合 788.97 亿元人民币），同比增长 28.82% 自由现金流：77.87 亿美元（现汇率约合 521.05 亿元人民币），同比增长 8.44% 基本每股收益：5.92 美元（现汇率约合 39.61 元人民币），同比增长 10.45% 稀释每股收益：5.85 美元（现汇率约合 39.14 元人民币），同比增长 11.01% 2026 财年第三财季 营业总收入：171.03 亿美元（现汇率约合 1144.42 亿元人民币），同比增长 5% 毛利润：97.14 亿美元（现汇率约合 649.99 亿元人民币），同比增长 4% 毛利率：56.8% 归母净利润：21.9 亿美元（现汇率约合 146.54 亿元人民币），同比增长 26% 经营现金流：40.25 亿美元（现汇率约合 269.33 亿元人民币），同比增长 30.64% 自由现金流：30.27 亿美元（现汇率约合 202.55 亿元人民币），同比增长 27.56% 基本每股收益：2.32 美元（现汇率约合 15.52 元人民币），同比增长 24.06% 稀释每股收益：2.31 美元（现汇率约合 15.46 元人民币），同比增长 26% AI 解读 本次501.82 亿美元（现汇率约合 3357.84 亿元人民币）营收超出市场预期，IBM九个月营收和利润均实现同比增长，AI业务推进顺利带动整体业绩提速。公司主营业务与财报亮点IBM是全球领先的信息技术和咨询公司，主营业务涵盖软件、咨询、基础设施、融资四大板块，当前重点推进Generative AI（GenAI）业务布局。九个月累计实现营业收入 501.82 亿美元（现汇率约合 3357.84 亿元人民币），同比增长约 5%；净收入达到 55.71 亿美元（现汇率约合 372.77 亿元人民币），持续保持增长；经营活动现金流净额为 117.91 亿美元（现汇率约合 788.97 亿元人民币），同比提升；自由现金流达到 77.87 亿美元（现汇率约合 521.05 亿元人民币），同比增长超过 6 亿美元（现汇率约合 40.15 亿元人民币）。分板块来看：软件板块营收 226.17 亿美元（现汇率约合 1513.37 亿元人民币），同比增长 8.1%；咨询板块营收 159.34 亿美元（现汇率约合 1066.19 亿元人民币），同比增长 1.5%；基础设施板块营收 108.68 亿美元（现汇率约合 727.21 亿元人民币），同比增长 2.7%；融资板块营收 5.98 亿美元（现汇率约合 40.01 亿元人民币），同比增长 7.3%。未来展望公司维持2026财年固定汇率营收增长预期在 4%-5%区间，同时上调全年自由现金流预期，预计全年自由现金流将同比增加超过 10 亿美元（现汇率约合 66.91 亿元人民币），对全年业绩保持乐观。股息信息IBM董事会批准季度现金股息为 1.69 美元（现汇率约合 11.31 元人民币） 每股，公司自1916年以来已连续每年派发季度股息，分红稳定性突出。 相关阅读： 《SpaceX 2026 财年第三财季归母净利润 44.04 亿美元，同比扭亏为盈》 《超微电脑 2027 财年第一财季预计营收 185 亿-195 亿美元，高于此前预期》 《IBM 2026 财年第二财季归母净利润 21.65 亿美元，同比下降 1.32%》 《IBM 2026 财年第二财季营收 172 亿美元，同比增长 1%》 风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，雷蛇（Razer）今晚正式发布了全新的北海巨妖萌猫版 V3 有线 RGB 游戏耳机，官方售价 799 元，10 月 26 日发货。该产品面向游戏直播与内容创作者，搭载可交互的猫耳 RGB 灯效、雷蛇 TriForce 40 毫米驱动单元以及 HyperClear 灵晰技术心形指向麦克风，支持即插即用 USB Type-C 连接，兼容 PC 及移动设备。IT之家从官方获悉，这款耳机配备 1680 万色 Razer Chroma RGB 灯效系统，猫耳与耳罩区域支持灯光自定义。通过 Razer Streamer Companion 应用，灯效可随直播提醒、弹幕及聊天互动实时变化。此外，这款耳机支持三条板载灯光预设，用户可在展会、漫展及线下聚会等场景中连接移动电源，保持 RGB 灯效持续点亮，并快速切换色彩与特效。在音频方面，这款耳机采用 40 毫米三频独立驱动单元，官方称其可提供更清晰、细节更丰富的声音分离表现，帮助用户区分游戏内提示音、语音通话及背景音频；耳机同时支持 7.1 环绕声效，提供沉浸式定位音频体验。麦克风方面，它配备了雷蛇经典的 Razer HyperClear 心形指向麦克风，可优先捕捉使用者语音，同时抑制背景噪音，适用于直播、语音聊天及社区互动场景。

articles.title: 苹果公布 Apple Music 全新品牌标识，创作灵感来自声音振动、声波实拍
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，苹果音乐（Apple Music）官方今日宣布推出全新身份标识。此次设计以“Made by Sound”（由声音塑造）为核心概念，邀请英国音乐制作人 Fred again.. 与 NEST Acoustics 共同参与，将声音振动转化为可视化的图形效果。据 Wallpaper* 报道，Apple Music 制作团队先创作了一段音乐，再通过换能器将声音转化为物理振动，使浅层矿物油表面产生波纹。团队全程通过摄像机记录液体的运动与折射效果，并将这些影像用于设计 Apple Music 的新视觉形象。苹果在介绍视频时称，这是一段关于音乐、协作与工艺的创作过程，最终效果完全通过实拍影像捕捉，而非单纯依靠数字特效生成。此次更新也涉及 Apple Music 的文字标识和音符图形。新文字标识保留苹果标志，并采用苹果自有字体 SF Pro 的定制版本，以更粗的字重和全小写的“music”呈现；重新设计的音符图标则借鉴了声音振动形成的视觉形态。IT之家注意到，苹果此前已在伦敦 Apple Music Hall 的宣传材料中使用新标识。9to5Mac 10 月 5 日报道称，新标识随后出现在 iOS 27.2 和 macOS 27.2 的测试版本中；苹果音乐应用图标也在后续测试版中出现黑白配色等变化。相关阅读：《苹果 iOS 27.2 引入新 Apple Music LOGO：加粗字体，全小写排版》

articles.title: NASA 公布月球探测车最新进展：VIPER 计划 2027 年探测月球南极水冰资源
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）当地时间 10 月 20 日公布了月球探测车最新研发进展及任务规划。NASA 表示，用于探测月球水冰等资源的“挥发物调查极地探索车”（VIPER）计划于 2027 年前往月球南极地区，载人月球地形车（LTV）则计划于 2028 年运抵月球南极地区，为未来载人探月任务和月球基地建设提供支持。据 NASA 官方公告，VIPER 目前已在美国约翰逊航天中心完成组装，正在进行最后阶段的测试，之后将转运至肯尼迪航天中心，为发射做准备。IT之家查询获悉，该探测车计划搭乘蓝色起源的第二艘“蓝月”MK1 月球着陆器前往月球，预计于 2027 年底抵达月球南极地区。VIPER 的主要任务是在月球南极地区寻找水冰及其他挥发性资源，并绘制相关资源分布图。NASA 计划让探测车进入永久阴影陨坑开展调查，研究不同深度、温度和土壤环境中的资源情况，为评估月球原位资源利用潜力提供数据。NASA 表示，相关探测结果也将帮助研究人员了解月球水资源的来源与分布，并为未来长期月面活动提供参考。载人月球地形车方面，NASA 表示，已选择 Astrolab 和 Lunar Outpost 参与首阶段月球地形车研发，并计划通过商业合作方式将车辆送往月球南极地区。蓝色起源将承担相关月球运输任务，目标是在 2028 年交付车辆。NASA 介绍，载人月球地形车属于不加压月面车辆，可搭载宇航员和货物，在宇航员执行舱外活动时提供地面交通支持。在载人任务到达前，这些车辆还可由地球远程操控，用于绘制月面地形图、收集环境数据，并测试车辆在极端温度、光照变化和永久阴影区域中的运行能力。NASA 表示，机器人探测车与载人月球地形车将共同支持月球基地建设的早期阶段。前者侧重于调查水冰等资源，后者则用于月面运输、科学调查和环境测绘，相关数据将为未来月球表面移动系统及基础设施设计提供依据。

articles.title: 英伟达 DGX Spark 支持 8 台集群：128GB 版本统一内存最高达 1TB，RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 相关任务提速 40%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，英伟达今日在柏林 GTC 2026 大会上宣布，DGX Spark 此前支持最多 4 台设备组建集群，目前已开放手动配置最多 8 台设备组建集群。如果是以 128GB 版本组建，其统一内存容量最高可达 1TB。同时，英伟达还发布了本地 AI 平台更新，并宣布与 llama.cpp、vLLM 开源社区合作优化 AI 推理性能，在特定工作负载下，RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 的推理性能最高提升 40%，DGX Spark 和 DGX Station 也分别获得最高 30% 和 20% 的性能提升。英伟达表示，4,999 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 33,450 元人民币）的 DGX Spark 的 64GB 版本将于 10 月 23 日开始通过合作伙伴陆续发售。针对集群部署，英伟达 Sync Model Launcher 计划于本月晚些时候上线，用户可通过该工具下载与硬件配置相匹配的模型和容器，并将模型连接至 OpenCode。工具还将自动加载 DGX Spark Skills，为设备故障排查、维护及工作流程提供指导。软件更新方面，10 月版 DGX Spark 更新加入 Wi-Fi 助手，允许设备在 appliance mode 下切换无线网络；DGX Spark Skills 也将通过 OpenCode 集成至英伟达 Sync，为日常维护和故障排查提供支持。模型方面，英伟达宣布支持更多可在本地运行的 AI 模型，包括 Nemotron、GLM、DeepSeek、Qwen、MiniMax 以及 FLUX.3 Klein 等，覆盖智能体、编程、图像生成和编辑等任务。英伟达还推出针对本地 AI 硬件优化的 Recursive Flint 编程模型。该模型采用混合专家（MoE）架构，总参数量为 400 亿，激活参数量为 25 亿。英伟达称，该模型在配备 64GB 内存的 RTX Spark 上推理速度超过每秒 220 个词元。针对本地运行大型模型时的内存压力，英伟达还发布了一组优化内存使用的模型检查点，通过量化降低内存占用，同时尽可能保持接近全精度模型的准确性。其中，Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local 可在单台 128GB DGX Spark 或 RTX PRO 6000 上运行；GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local 则面向两台系统的配置。推理性能优化是此次更新的另一项重点。根据英伟达公布的数据，在 llama.cpp 中，针对 Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 的多 token 预测（MTP）推测解码优化，可使 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 上的端到端智能体任务提速最高 1.4 倍；在 vLLM 中，针对 Qwen3.8 27B 的推测解码和 FlashInfer 预填充内核优化，可使 DGX Spark 上的相关任务提速最高 1.3 倍；DGX Station 运行 GLM 5.3 Flash 时，吞吐量最高提升至原来的 1.2 倍。英伟达还公布了 DGX Station 的企业管理与应用扩展计划，包括新增 Absolute Security、思科旗下 Splunk、Microsoft Intune、Tanium 等七项管理集成，帮助企业部署和管理本地 AI 基础设施。DGX Station 的 Windows 版本预计于 12 月推出，将支持制造业相关应用，以及设计、仿真、验证和工程自动化工作流。此外，英伟达计划为 DGX Station 推出开放源代码机器人参考工作流，并以早期访问形式提供 NVIDIA Cloud Functions，让团队通过统一接口共享本地模型服务。相关阅读：《英伟达黄仁勋：已测超 1200 款应用，RTX Spark 是全球唯一本地原生运行所有应用的电脑》《桌面 AI 超算新选择：英伟达 NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB 内存版正式发布，4999 美元》

articles.title: OPPO 推出 Find X10 全球版手机：电池相比国行版缩减 850mAh，缺少 16GB+1TB 版本
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，OPPO 今日在海外市场推出 Find X10 全球版手机。新机采用 6.59 英寸 AMOLED 屏幕、双 2 亿影像和天玑 9600M 芯片。12GB+256GB 版本售价为 1,099 英镑（IT之家注：现汇率约合 9,819 元人民币）/1,299 欧元（现汇率约合 9,752 元人民币）。据介绍，OPPO Find X10 全球版配备 6.59 英寸 LTPO AMOLED 屏幕，分辨率为 2768 × 1272 像素，边框宽度 0.99 毫米，支持 144Hz 高刷，HDR 峰值亮度可达 3600 尼特。规格方面，该机搭载联发科天玑 9600M 芯片，采用台积电 3nm 工艺打造。搭配 12GB LPDDR5X 内存，最高可选 512GB UFS 4.1 存储。影像方面，该机配备 2 亿像素 1/1.4 英寸三星 ISOCELL HPE 主摄，以及 2 亿像素 1/1.56 英寸 ISOCELL HP5 长焦，还有 5000 万像素 ISOCELL JN5 超广角，前摄同样是 50MP JN5。新机支持 Lumo 真彩影像，让色彩、肤色更加自然。主摄和长焦支持 4K 120FPS 或 8K 30FPS 录像。此外，这款手机配备 7150mAh 硅碳负极电池，支持 80W 有线快充、50W 无线充电。参考IT之家此前报道，Find X10 国行版采用 8000mAh 电池，全球版与之相比缩减 850mAh，且缺少 16GB+1TB 高配版本。

articles.title: 腾讯内测 AI 互动社区“懂了鸭”：一句话生成可玩的动态课件与 3D 演示
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，今日有用户反馈，腾讯正在内测一款面向少儿与青少年的 AI 互动内容社区“懂了鸭”，官方网站（dongleya.qq.com）与微信小程序均已上线，目前向亲子用户和一线教师开放小范围测试。该产品的核心载体是“奇妙卡”，一种可拖拽、可模拟、可操作的交互式内容单元，家长、教师或知识创作者输入自然语言描述，即可借助内置 AI 智能体生成 3D 演示、动态课件、互动绘本、轻量游戏或记忆卡等作品，无需编程基础。用户既可以浏览社区中已有的奇妙卡作品，也可以对他人作品进行二次改编。从公开信息看，懂了鸭在产品形态上尝试将“内容消费”与“内容生产”放在同一个社区内完成。首页按学前、小学、初中、高中四个学段以及健康、语言、数学、科学、艺术、信息科技等学科领域组织内容。在创作侧，聊天机器人接受文字或语音输入，将想法转化为作品后发布到社区，形成“AI 降低制作门槛、社区承接分发”的循环。网经社的报道将这一机制概括为“输入创意想法，借助内置 AI Agent，无需代码即可一键生成”，并指出平台同时覆盖亲子互动、K12 课堂和课外探索三类场景。IT之家注意到，懂了鸭在模型列表中列出的可选模型包括 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、DeepSeek V4 Pro、DeepSeek V4 Flash、Hy3、Hy4 preview、MiniMax M3、Kimi K3 和 GLM-5.3 等。对于一款面向未成年人的教育类产品，多模型策略的意义可能不止于“给用户更多选择”：不同模型在生成 3D 演示、动态课件或叙事绘本时的能力侧重不同，按任务类型路由到合适的模型，是提升生成质量与稳定性的现实路径。在此之前，腾讯已在 AI 助手、AI 编程、AI 搜索等方向有多条产品线在推进，而面向 K12 与亲子场景的互动内容社区尚属空白。与字节“豆包爱学”聚焦拍照答疑、作业批改、错题分析等“解题 — 批改 — 答疑”闭环不同，懂了鸭的重心在“造内容”：让教师和家长成为互动学习材料的制作者，让孩子在可操作、可模拟的环境中接触知识，而非直接给出答案。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，在今年 9 月 7 日的 HarmonyOS 7 | HUAWEI Mate XT 2 及全场景新品发布会上，鸿蒙 7 操作系统正式发布。在发布会现场，华为还剧透了全新功能 —— 小艺 AI 快捷栏。官方 PPT 页面显示，该功能开启后，小艺将在手机桌面底部的 Dock 栏常驻。本月早些时候，华为客户服务透露该功能预计在 10 月底逐步和大家见面。IT之家今日再次就该功能的上线时间进行了询问，对方表示：该功能预计将在 11 月初逐步和大家见面。届时会根据机型分批推送，请您留意系统更新提示。据华为客户服务介绍，小艺 AI 快捷栏是 HarmonyOS 7 的新功能，开启 AI 快捷栏后 AI 将在快捷栏显示，点击可探索更多 AI 服务。相关阅读：《华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 7 操作系统正式发布：全新空间美学设计语言，搭载系统智能体小艺》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，开源 JavaScript 运行时环境 Node.js 今日针对 26.x、24.x 和 22.x 系列版本发布安全更新，修复 10 余个安全漏洞，包含 4 个高危漏洞。IT之家附本次更新修复漏洞如下：dns.resolve 会截断包含 NUL 字符的域名（CVE-2026-105482）—— 高危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 hasanfleyah 的报告，并感谢 jasnell 修复该问题。当 IP 地址使用全角数字表示时，可绕过 TLS 证书主机名验证（CVE-2026-105483）—— 高危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x 和 24.x。感谢 hasanfleyah 的报告，并感谢 jasnell 修复该问题。当主机名通过宽松解析可被解析为 IP 地址时，可绕过 TLS 证书主机名验证（CVE-2026-106069）—— 高危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 anagnorisis2peripeteia 的报告，并感谢 mcollina 修复该问题。Node.js Brotli 解码器存在越界写入漏洞，可导致远程代码执行（CVE-2026-111497）—— 高危Node.js 存在一项缺陷，其 Brotli 解码器可能发生越界写入，从而导致远程代码执行。该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 mcollina 的报告，并感谢 aduh95 修复该问题。Keep-alive 套接字会处理在请求发送前就已写入的响应（CVE-2026-105481）—— 中危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 hasanfleyah 报告此漏洞，并感谢 jasnell 修复该问题。对非规范 IPv4 主机名的证书验证不正确，导致 DNS SAN 可用于验证 IP 端点（CVE-2026-106072）—— 中危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 br41ny 报告此漏洞，并感谢 mcollina 修复该问题。crypto.randomUUID () 和 randomInt () 的熵缓存被保存到用户态启动快照和 SEA 中，导致每个进程重复生成相同的值（CVE-2026-106074）—— 中危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 gesposito 报告此漏洞，并感谢 panva 修复该问题。Node.js ZipFile 在 ZIP 文件头验证失败后仍会返回由攻击者控制的前缀字节（CVE-2026-106070）—— 低危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x。感谢 startimeash 报告此漏洞，并感谢 mcollina 修复该问题。权限模型通过通配符基数查找机制授予过多文件系统权限（CVE-2026-106071）—— 低危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x。感谢 malikhamzaiqbal 报告此漏洞，并感谢 jasnell 修复该问题。可通过 fs.realpathSync 绕过权限模型（CVE-2026-106073）—— 低危该漏洞影响 Node.js 26.x、24.x 和 22.x。感谢 0xoroot 报告此漏洞，并感谢 RafaelGSS 修复该问题。下载链接：Node.js v22.23.4Node.js v24.22.1Node.js v26.12.1

articles.title: 宁德时代回应“投资者对明年行业需求担忧”：2027 年行业需求依旧可期，没有市场预期的那么悲观
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，据证券时报今日报道，近期部分投资者对明年新能源行业需求有些担心。对此，宁德时代回应称，从公司角度看，2027 年行业需求依旧可以期待。国内乘用车方面，尽管今年乘用车整体销量有所下降，但可以看到电动化率在快速提升，并且单车带电量有较快提升，所以国内新能源乘用车动力电池的增速依然实现了正增长。国内新能源商用车的电动化率也在快速提升；欧洲的电动化趋势具有连续性，不断有竞争力的新车型推出；其他市场的电动化潜力可能被市场低估。储能方面，无论是国内还是海外都保持着不错的增速，特别是海外部分市场的储能需求比较旺盛。整体而言，全球动力及储能电池的市场需求可能没有市场预期的那么悲观，仍有不错的增长潜力。对于产能利用率的问题，宁德时代回应称，上半年公司产能利用率非常饱和。近年来公司根据市场需求加快产能建设进度，随着今年产能的陆续投产，产能紧张程度有所缓解。但市场需求也在持续增长，整体而言，接下来产能利用率仍将处于较高水平，保持较健康的状态。IT之家附宁德时代 2026 年三季度（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）报告数据：营业总收入：1652.21 亿元，同比增长 58.58%归母净利润：212.46 亿元，同比增长 14.54%扣非净利润：188.62 亿元，同比增长 14.86%加权平均净资产收益率：5.56%基本每股收益：4.62 元，同比增长 12.68%稀释每股收益：4.62 元，同比增长 12.68%

articles.title: 黄仁勋发布 AI“预制工厂”DSX POD：最快 14 天部署投产，英伟达计划 2027 年初全球交付
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋今日在德国柏林举行的 GTC 大会上宣布推出模块化 AI 工厂参考设计 DSX POD，面向以 Vera Rubin 平台为核心的完整 AI 工厂系统。英伟达表示，该方案将计算、网络、布线、机架供电、液冷管路安装及功能验证等工作提前转移至工厂完成，计划于 2027 年初通过合作伙伴在全球交付。DSX POD 的核心思路是将 AI 基础设施预先集成到“模块化集装箱”中，并在发货前完成系统集成与验证。设备抵达部署现场后，客户只需将其接入已经准备就绪的电力、冷却、网络等配套设施，即可开展后续部署。英伟达称，这种方式能够减少传统数据中心建设过程中复杂的现场施工、专业人员协调和物流工作，并降低现场安装错误及零部件交付延误带来的影响。英伟达表示，在部署场地及配套基础设施已经准备就绪的情况下，DSX POD 可将基础设施部署周期从传统方式的约 6 个月缩短至最短 14 天。黄仁勋表示，AI 工厂只有在开始产生 token 时才能创造价值，而不仅仅是在建设完成时。英伟达称，DSX POD 旨在缩短基础设施从现场准备就绪到开始运行生产级 AI 工作负载的时间，使运营商能够更早提供推理服务并获得收入。合作伙伴方面，英伟达正在与戴尔科技、惠普企业、联想、技嘉、鸿海旗下工业富联、和硕、广达旗下云达科技（QCT）、纬创、施耐德电气、维谛技术等企业合作，推动 DSX POD 的制造、集成和交付。英伟达表示，全球合作伙伴计划于 2027 年初开始交付相关 AI 工厂系统。相关阅读：《英伟达联合思灵推出人形机器人参考平台 Agile ONE SN，计划 2027 年初上市》《英伟达黄仁勋称未来电信运营商都将提供 AI 算力，电信基站有望发展成分布式 AI 网络》《奔驰与英伟达合作开发城市辅助驾驶系统 MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO，计划年底在德国向部分用户开放》

articles.title: 谷歌 CEO 桑达尔 · 皮查伊：公司正牺牲云业务短期收入支持前沿 AI 研发，2027 年算力难以锁定
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，谷歌首席执行官桑达尔 · 皮查伊今日表示，公司正将部分算力从云业务转向前沿 AI 研发，以全力支持前沿 AI 发展。对谷歌而言，开发前沿 AI 成本高昂，需要耗费大量计算资源和芯片，但这些资源原本可以拿给云业务高价出售。皮查伊对此表示，将资源投入前沿人工智能研发是谷歌的“根本所在”。这名 CEO 还表示，若客户目前寻求锁定 2027 年算力，将面临极大困难，原因包括数据中心从决策到投运需两至三年，以及智能体任务需求激增。他解释称：“我们的云业务在任何特定时刻都能放弃短期收入，因为我们正做出计算方面的权衡，以支持前沿 AI 发展。”

articles.title: OpenAI 联手 PerturbAI：让近 2000 个 AI 智能体一起搞科研，加速新药研发
articles.content: 北京时间 10 月 21 日，生物技术公司 PerturbAI 宣布与 OpenAI 合作的最新进展。双方联合斯克里普斯研究所（Scripps Research）开发了一套 AI 推理框架，通过近 2000 个 AI 智能体并行工作，帮助科学家分析复杂生物实验数据、检索文献，并提出可供后续实验检验的假说。据 PerturbAI 介绍，这套系统在分析其全脑基因组图谱时，用 32 分钟完成数据分析与研究发现整合。公司估计，如果由人类按串行方式开展分析和文献审阅，相关工作可能需要数月至一年。这一时间对比来自公司估算，并非与人类团队开展的同期对照测试。在具体流程中，AI 智能体分别分析细胞反应、搜索科学文献，将实验结果与已有生物学知识联系起来，再汇总形成“推理图谱”，串联基因、细胞反应、既有研究及可能的生物学机制，为科学家提供进一步调查的线索。研究团队还邀请生物学专家，从新颖性、证据支持程度、后续研究优先级和置信度等方面评估报告。在与单个 AI 智能体生成报告的盲评比较中，专家有 75% 的时候更偏好多智能体系统给出的解释。这一结果反映的是专家对报告的偏好，不能直接理解为研究结论的准确率。此次分析使用的数据来自 PerturbAI 今年 3 月公布的全脑 CRISPR 图谱，涵盖约 800 万个细胞。公司称，该图谱在数月内生成，目前下载量已超过 4 万次。此后，PerturbAI 还构建了覆盖代谢疾病和衰老研究的专有图谱。双方的合作已持续约一年，接下来将利用 PerturbAI 在活体系统中生成的因果生物学数据，联合开展新药靶点发现。相关成果已通过联合预印本和博客公布，目前披露的结果主要涉及数据解读及研究假说生成，所提出线索仍需后续实验验证。

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26887v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. We introduce Navalia, a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training. Using corporate financial reports as its data source, Navalia semantically selects supporting evidence from complete fact sets and constructs executable computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable evidence and actual data dependencies between steps. articles.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26904v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent studies have proposed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) methods that enable LLMs to generate high-quality RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Existing approaches optimize circuit PPA (Power, Performance, Area) by aggregating multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, making it difficult to simultaneously generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions across different trade-offs such as low power, low latency, and small area. However, in practical design, the relative importance of each objective varies depending on product requirements and design constraints; thus, obtaining a diverse and high-quality candidate set is beneficial in that designers can choose a preferred trade-off a posteriori. articles.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26913v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. articles.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26924v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verifying analytical results both during evolution and after task assembly. articles.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are enabling agents to move beyond predefined workflows toward autonomous planning and execution, creating new opportunities for smart manufacturing. However, dynamic environments, complex physical constraints, and stringent reliability requirements hinder the direct deployment of general-purpose agents in smart manufacturing. This article presents a systematic overview of LLM-driven industrial agents. First, we analyze five key challenges and discuss the concept and core characteristics of industrial agents. We then establish a unified taxonomy covering application scenarios, embodiment forms, and five capability levels. Next, we propose a four-layer system architecture and detail its core modules and operational mechanisms for closed-loop task execution. Abstract: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conversational recommender systems have recently adopted vision-language models to match user dialogue intents with multimodal product information. However, extending these methods to many product domains faces a dilemma: deploying a separately adapted VLM per domain scales cost linearly with the number of domains and requires routing each dialogue to the right model, while naively merging all domains into a single VLM degrades accuracy because product characteristics vary widely across categories. We propose LightCRS, a lightweight, query-conditioned framework for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. LightCRS precomputes multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) struggle with classical planning, but benchmarks rarely distinguish structural difficulty from the difficulty of interpreting symbolic vocabulary. We examine seven STRIPS domains with BFS-optimal plan lengths. ARC also fails to outperform a linear model using the same features. To isolate semantic effects, we progressively rename predicates while preserving states, transitions, and optimal plans. articles.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on reusable skills. However, scaling skill libraries makes efficient and accurate skill use difficult. Full skill loading incurs high token and runtime overhead. In contrast, flat semantic retrieval treats skills as independent text entries, ignoring dependencies, execution order, state transitions, and data flow constraints. We propose SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework for efficient skill use in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions derived from successful executions. For a new task, SPEM reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates when available. Otherwise, it retrieves atomic skills and invokes Skill-GNN for state- and structure-aware skill selection. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have recently demonstrated outstanding performance in single-turn tasks, yet they continue to struggle with long-horizon tasks, particularly in environments without prior training. A key limitation of single LLMs is their difficulty in processing long contexts, which stems from weaknesses in continuous decision-making and reasoning capabilities. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27045v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. It develops the foundations of physical AI across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems begin to resolve open research problems, reliable verification becomes increasingly important. Formal mathematics provides a trusted framework for mathematical reasoning, enabling agents to produce machine-checkable proofs while conducting mathematical exploration. Existing formal mathematics benchmarks often focus on known results or a small set of prominent open problems, which can become difficult to evaluate reliably once solutions are discovered and widely disseminated. Existing evaluation protocols are also not always aligned with how modern coding agents operate. We therefore introduce ReuF2F, a Lean 4 benchmark of 244 formalized open problems drawn from Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), spanning entry-level open research problems across a broad range of mathematical subfields. Abstract: Clinical care, health-system operations and biomedical discovery depend on extracting reliable answers from patient records, yet applying diverse clinical questions across entire populations remains computationally expensive. Here we present Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter decision model for fast, typed judgments from clinical records, along with two agentic harnesses in which CS1 works together with a generalist language model. CS1-4B is trained on 12.4 million questions and answers from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system, combining structured-data keys, observed outcomes and language-model supervision across clinical notes, diagnostic reports and patient timelines. It answers multiple typed questions in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, and each answer carries a probability that can route uncertain cases to human review. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents act on the external world through tools and third-party skills, so a single executed action can cause irreversible harm. Existing defenses judge a proposed action without tracking whether its content comes from the user or from external sources such as tool outputs, and they judge it in isolation rather than against an available alternative, which forces a trade-off between security and utility. We present PROVISO, a controller that decides which action to commit after the agent proposes an action and before it is executed. PROVISO encodes trusted observations, external observations, the proposed action, and an alternative into provenance-typed memory, relates them through role-specific queries, and commits the action with the highest calibrated value learned from outcomes. articles.title: PORA: Learning When More Reasoning Pays Off for LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27119v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents perform tasks over multiple steps and revise their actions based on feedback. As the total reasoning budget is often limited and must support future steps, the agent must choose between short and long reasoning before each action. Longer reasoning may improve the final task outcome by preventing later errors, but it also uses budget capacity that may be needed for future decisions. This creates two challenges: estimating the downstream value of long reasoning and deciding when that value is worth using the remaining budget. We propose Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), which learns this decision by comparing short and long reasoning from the same interaction state. During training, \method{} completes the task twice from each selected state, once with a short reasoning allowance and once with a long allowance, and compares their final quality and total processing to estimate when longer reasoning is valuable. Abstract: Pluralistic alignment requires AI systems to learn from diverse populations whose preferences may reflect heterogeneous or even conflicting objectives, and to personalize their behavior to individual users. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in non-verifiable domains such as financial services, where they must interpret user intent, rewrite queries, and retrieve information under domain-specific constraints. Abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Abstract: Scientific foundation models increasingly operate on continuous phenomena, yet still use discrete residual computation. Its hidden states evolve through an ordinary differential equation evaluated by higher-order numerical integration, with solver order and step size controlling computation. Across eight scientific tasks, Continuum-LM trains stably and improves mean exact-match accuracy by 7.77 and 10.96 percentage points over discrete counterparts at the 0.6B and 1.7B scales, respectively. Abstract: We show that two-layer transformers trained to near-zero loss on a sorting task converge to one of two mechanistically distinct solution classes depending on their initialization. articles.content:

Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains a language model by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27030v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Indirect and noisy observations are difficult to invert when the forward operator smooths out the unknown signal. In this case, the unstable modes are precisely the modes that the data reveals least, thus the success of any reconstruction method depends on how prior information interacts with the geometry of the operator across regularity scales. Diffusion priors have become ubiquitous for such problems; however, the current theory still does not determine when a learned score remains informative under ill-posed forward operators. In this paper, we study posterior diffusion for linear inverse problems on Hilbert scales and derive a stability theory under an explicit score-amplification condition. Abstract: We introduce Lookup-table (LUT)-aware Efficient Attention on FPGAs (LEAF). LEAF is the first nanosecond-scale LUT-aware transformer for FPGAs. Deploying transformers that are large enough to perform well, small enough to fit on an FPGA, and fast enough to meet the sub-microsecond timescales required by real-time systems such as those at CERN remains difficult, since the same attention mechanism that gives these models their high expressivity also makes them costly to implement in hardware. articles.title: ClockMark: Adaptive and Host-Dependent Watermarking for Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) watermarking operates on the next-token distribution that evolves during generation. In streaming generation, each sampled token becomes part of the text and affects subsequent distributions. Embedding therefore proceeds with a changing host, unlike classical watermarking, which adapts embedding to an existing host signal. To accommodate this difference, we formulate a novel embedding framework for LLM watermarking based on two principles. We first argue that embedding should be adaptive, retaining the state of previous sampling decisions to better guide subsequent choices. We further argue that embedding should be host-dependent, using the current LLM distribution to constrain both token selection and state updates. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27107v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Credit card fraud is a significant problem for financial institutions, resulting in substantial monetary loss each year. Fraud patterns and methods are continuously evolving, with fraudulent transactions often disguised to resemble legitimate activity. Real world transaction data for fraud detection is severely affected by class imbalance making it harder to detect these transactions. Fraudulent transactions are rarely isolated. Accounts, devices, and other common attributes are often shared across fraudulent activity, revealing relational patterns that individual transaction features alone cannot capture. Graph-based approaches model these relationships explicitly. However, standard graph neural networks aggregate neighbourhood information uniformly, which can dilute the already scarce signal carried by fraudulent transactions and limit detection of camouflaged fraud. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse expert activation, but deployment still requires storing a large number of expert parameters. We study post-training expert pruning using task-domain calibration data as a subset-selection problem: given a pretrained MoE layer, select a fixed number of experts that best reconstruct its original output. Exact subset search is combinatorial and becomes intractable for modern MoE models with many experts per layer. We develop OptEP, a scalable continuous relaxation that directly optimizes differentiable expert-selection variables, followed by a lightweight reconstruction-based update of the retained expert weights. Across multiple MoE architectures and tasks spanning mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approach improves over the strongest existing expert-pruning baselines, with absolute accuracy gains of up to 15.05% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 14.55% on Qwen3-235B-A22B, 11

Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is challenging long-held assumptions in active flow control. By learning directly from interaction with a flow, DRL agents can find actuation strategies for nonlinear, unsteady flows without explicit models, often exploiting mechanisms that classical control would not anticipate. High-speed flows are a demanding test of this promise: shocks, shock/boundary-layer interactions, transition, aerothermal loading and microsecond-scale dynamics strain both algorithms and hardware. Yet most demonstrations remain idealized, low-speed simulations with limited evidence of robustness, interpretability, transferability or experimental deployment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27139v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We encounter a system through its responses, yet its state concerns how the system is. Predicting further responses promises knowledge beyond what is immediately observed. What that knowledge tells us about the system's state depends on what we mean by a state in the first place. We give this notion a model-relative meaning: a state is the complete response profile over a specified query universe, and configurations agreeing on every query are regarded as the same state. From this perspective, a learned state is understood through the distinctions between these profiles that it retains. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26864v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gradient ascent (GA) is a simple language-model unlearning baseline, but it continues increasing forget loss after useful forgetting has occurred. This unbounded pressure can damage retained utility and make forgotten examples abnormally high-loss. We introduce H2DF, a calibrated target-band objective that applies GA-like pressure below a data-dependent lower target and suppresses, or reverses, that pressure after the target region is reached. The targets are estimated from matched non-member examples before training, so the base objective requires one forget-batch forward/backward pass per optimization step; our reported TOFU variant adds sparse retain replay every tenth step. We instantiate a one-sided objective for TOFU question answering and a two-sided objective for MUSE-News language modeling. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented speech translation improves rare terminology, but systems such as RASST still assume that users provide a glossary before each session. That assumption is inconvenient for live talks, while merging every domain into one growing glossary eventually places too many irrelevant terms in the same retrieval and prompt competition. We present AutoTerm-SST, an interactive system that removes session-time glossary upload and domain selection. It organizes a large offline terminology catalog into topic slices, matches recent streaming translation context to bilingual slice prototypes, and activates a compact multi-slice working set under fixed retrieval and prompt budgets. On five ACL and five ESO oncology talks, AutoTerm matches a known-domain reference in terminology accuracy (88.3% vs. 88.1%) and mWER-resegmented BLEU (45.09 vs. 45.19), while requiring no domain input. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern speech systems are evolving into ecosystems of autonomous speech agents that speak together, negotiate, and trade assets such as embeddings, spectrograms, or raw data. In such markets, sellers cannot reveal assets for evaluation due to privacy constraints, and buyers cannot price what they cannot test. Thus, we open-source WaveCommitments, an end-to-end design that pairs confidential asset valuation via Data Shapley inside a trusted execution environment with multivariate polynomial commitments. It enables selective openings and tamper-evident provenance to prove that a delivered asset matches the valuation while hiding everything else. Our extensive experiments across three known datasets and various tasks with state-of-the-art encoders, including Whisper, reveal that we speed up the best benchmarks by up to 20x while reducing their proof sizes by up to 39x. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26868v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are subtle behavioural states that can be expressed through both what a person says and how it is spoken. This paper presents an audio--text framework for video-level A/H recognition. Full-video transcripts and speech waveforms are encoded using pre-trained multilingual BERT and wav2vec~2.0, respectively, and projected into a shared representation space. Two stacked bidirectional cross-attention blocks allow linguistic tokens to attend to acoustic frames and acoustic frames to attend to linguistic context without requiring explicit temporal alignment. The resulting sequences are aggregated through masked mean pooling and combined using concatenation, element-wise products, and absolute differences for binary classification. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26888v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Mixture of Phonetic Experts based Low-Rank Adaptation (MoPE-LoRA), a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for accented English speech recognition. Recent mixture-of-experts approaches typically allocate experts per accent, implicitly treating accent identity as the primary axis of variation. In contrast, we organize adaptation along phonetic categories, motivated by the observation that accent differences are often expressed as systematic distortions of phoneme realization. MoPE-LoRA introduces a fixed set of six low-rank experts aligned with manner-of-articulation classes and performs frame-level routing through a hybrid mechanism that combines phoneme supervision with learned acoustic gating. Because the expert set is shared across accents, the model does not require accent-specific modules and naturally extends to previously unseen accents. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26926v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) possess broad factual knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but solving complex tasks also requires procedural knowledge about how to act. Existing approaches often represent procedural knowledge through trajectories or bundled skills, limiting flexible reuse across interaction histories. This paper introduces Procedural Atoms, fine-grained and independently applicable units that represent Intent, When, Do, and Avoid guidance. Building on this representation, we propose AtomSD, an Atom-guided Self-Distillation framework in which the learner continually extracts Procedural Atoms from its own successful trajectories and distills them into the evolving policy through Atom-conditioned supervision and task-reward optimization. articles.content:

Abstract: Large clinical language models often require multi-GPU infrastructure, limiting local deployment. We introduce CERTA, a decision-level statistical certificate that determines when a quantized model may substitute for its native BF16 reference and escalates decisions that cannot be certified to it. In the higher-power operational analysis, round-to-nearest 8-bit quantization at BF16 storage served 99.8-100% of held-out decisions across all eleven models; formal finite-sample guarantees were assessed separately using the exact split-sample procedure. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26952v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Relational triple extraction identifies entity relations from raw sentences without depending on entity type information. The performance of traditional methods is seriously degenerated by ``unseen'' entities, because these methods can't build contextual dependencies relevant ``unseen'' entities. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a multi-granularity interaction network that leverages word-word, entity-relation, and head-tail interactions to capture deep semantic dependencies. By incorporating multiple iterations, the multi-granularity interaction network is effective to refine the representations corresponding to head and tail entities. It enhances the global semantic features associated with relational triples, aiding in the remediation of triples that may have been overlooked or omitted in earlier steps. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon language agents require compact memories that retain interaction evidence while preserving competing hypotheses about unobserved states. Although effective, many belief-state methods encode memory in discrete natural language, where repeated compression can omit evidence or prematurely discard plausible alternatives. We introduce LAMB, a recurrent framework for latent multi-hypothesis beliefs. A Common--Delta factorization combines a shared Common state for interaction evidence with weighted Delta components for competing hypotheses. Relative evidence from action-outcome predictions guides recurrent hypothesis updates without generating textual memory. A context-conditioned readout exposes hypotheses separately to the policy through a fixed-token belief prefix in the default configuration. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26972v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present SZED's submission to ArGuard 2026 Track A: Arabic hateful meme detection. The task has two parts: binary classification (A1) and fine-grained multi-label tagging (A2). For A1, we fuse MARBERTv2 and CLIP ViT-L/14 embeddings, comparing concatenation, self-attention, and ensemble heads. For A2, we use a multi-task label-attention architecture with per-class query vectors and an auxiliary head for cascade calibration. We reach macro-F1 = 0.7597 on A1 and 0.3142 on A2 (averaged over 10 active classes). We report reproducibility across runs, per-class error patterns, and the effect of cascade calibration on the long-tailed A2 label space.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26976v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish sharp degree bounds for Putinar sum-of-squares (SOS) certificates in terms of the positivity margin $\delta$. For any fixed Archimedean quadratic module with prescribed generators and any fixed bound on the degree of the objective, we prove a uniform certificate-degree upper bound of $O(\delta^{-1/2}\log^2(2/\delta))$ for normalized polynomial objectives. We show that this bound is sharp by constructing a matching lower-bound example in three variables, thereby establishing that the dependence on $\delta$ is optimal. These matching bounds also yield sharp worst-case convergence rates for the Lasserre hierarchy.

Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing and artificial intelligence applications through their capabilities in reasoning, text generation and knowledge retrieval. Abstract: EHR foundation models promise scalable clinical prediction across health systems, yet their deployment is constrained by a tokenization bottleneck. The same clinical concept can appear as different ontology codes, local identifiers, synonyms, or free-text descriptions, which standard EHR tokenizers treat as unrelated symbols. Abstract: Creating photorealistic human heads typically involves trade-offs between representation power, efficiency, and generalizability. Traditional mesh-based solutions relying on 3DMMs generally sacrifice representation power but are efficient to render. On the other hand, NeRF-based methods improve representation power and fidelity while sacrificing efficiency. Gaussian splatting methods attempt to resolve these trade-offs by offering both high representation power and efficiency with real-time rendering. However, their efficiency nonetheless depends on the number of rasterized Gaussians, and the time needed to optimize and prepare the head (the enrollment time) is often high. Abstract: Long-video understanding often requires answering many questions about a single video whose evidence is distributed across extended temporal contexts. Conventional video-language models repeatedly encode frames or retrieve visual evidence for every question. Parameterized video memory offers a write-once alternative, but existing methods rely primarily on synthesized text and fixed adaptation configurations, leaving open where video knowledge should be written and how visual evidence should shape the memory. Abstract: Temperature-field reconstruction and prediction are important for condition monitoring, process analysis, and state assessment in industrial and dynamic environments. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26922v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Controllable object insertion provides a targeted approach to augmenting object detection datasets that require category--count fidelity, annotation alignment, and source-content preservation beyond visual realism. Several approaches have been proposed to address this grand challenge, but most suffer from different constraints in precise category--count requests and visual consistency, limited coordination across categories and instances, and poor localization of multiple objects of specific category and count. We design SceneP2F, a two-stage trainable framework that connects scene-aware joint planning with layout-aligned generation leveraging explicit instance-level layouts. SceneP2F consists of two novel designs. The first is ScenePlan which allocates one class-labeled query per requested instance, jointly predicts scene-compatible object centers, and separately estimates box sizes conditioned on the planned centers and scene context.

Abstract: An event camera emits events at a rate given by the scene motion, object texture, illumination, its own contrast thresholds, and other settings. Across the N-Caltech101 dataset, recorded by a single event camera, the event rate varies by roughly 26x. Standard event-based Graph Neural Network GNN pipelines do not make use of the variable event rate. They either normalize each event's timestamp into a fixed window or train the network to be invariant to the event rate. Abstract: When given an image and a text prompt, vision-language models (VLMs) can produce seemingly sophisticated text responses. To detect these hallucinations, certain methods interestingly leverage internal signals from the VLM as it generates the text response; potentially, these methods use the same signals that led to a hallucination to detect it. We conduct an in-depth analysis to understand the robustness of these detection methods. First, we show that a naive baseline of a generated word's token position in the VLM text response achieves competitive performance. Abstract: Recent advances in unified visual editing have begun to consolidate image and video editing within a single model, while 3D scene editing remains largely separate and constrained by scarce paired training data. Abstract: Generating human-object interactions (HOIs) with multiple objects is challenging because the resulting motions arise from different underlying causes. Human motion reflects semantic intent, intentionally manipulated objects must remain coordinated with the human, while surrounding objects move primarily as physical consequences of contact and collision. Our method first generates full-body human motion from text and scene context, then predicts trajectories for a small number of intentionally manipulated driver objects conditioned on the human motion. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27040v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose multimodal models, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, demonstrate broad capabilities in embodied manipulation. Our analysis indicates that this generality is accompanied by strong spatial perception, as Astra can determine where to interact with task-relevant entities amid visual distractors. Because spatial perception connects high-level reasoning to the physical scene, we investigate scaling visual grounding to strengthen the perceptual foundation of general embodied operation. Abstract: Reliable contact establishment remains a critical challenge for autonomous on-orbit servicing (OOS), particularly when interacting with non-cooperative targets. arXiv:2610.27162v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In robot-assisted education, a robot must understand how to complete a task in order to effectively guide a student through it. We present a novel method that enables a semi-autonomous, camera-equipped robot to recognise the task goal and plan actions to achieve it. Our work focuses on Shoebox Tasks, an activity commonly used in the education of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). These tasks are designed so that the goal can be inferred directly from their visual structure. We have developed a solver that uses a vision-based Large Language Model to convert photos of a Shoebox Task into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) representation and generate action plans for solving it. Abstract: Diffusion policies with linearly composed scores have emerged as a promising approach to multitask robotic learning by combining separate factors to enable modular, task-wise adaptation, compositional generalization, and interpretable functional decomposition. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27242v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid dexterous manipulation needs reference motions that are both semantically rich and kinematically feasible for the target robot. Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generators supply diverse, language-specified demonstrations, but they synthesize motion in human (MANO) space. The embodiment gap is therefore deferred to post-hoc retargeting, where trajectories deployed on the robot can fail to maintain contact with objects and also degrade policy learning. Our key idea is that robot reachability should constrain the interaction trajectories while they are being generated. We present EmbodyHOI, which runs a differentiable inverse-kinematics (IK) solver for a specific humanoid embodiment inside the sampling loop of a frozen flow-matching HOI trajectory generator. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Walking without vision requires timely, unambiguous guidance, yet many wearable aids encode directions as audio or vibrotactile signals that users must translate into movement. We present XoNav, a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders guidance cues directly at the hip joints. It renders an Advance cue and two-level Braking cues through sagittal-plane actuators and two-level Steering cues through frontal-plane actuators. A bilateral LSTM-based gait-state classifier uses two thigh-mounted IMUs to identify gait states, enabling haptic cues to be delivered in coordination with the wearer's gait while suppressing them during standing. The classifier generalized to unseen users with recalls of 95.2-97.9%, with mean detection delays of 38.6 and 63.1 ms for stance-to-swing and swing-to-stance transitions, respectively. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27275v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Maximum clique and maximum consensus are widely used formulations for robust point cloud registration in robotics. Maximum consensus seeks one transformation that aligns as many matches as possible, while maximum clique selects matches through pairwise distance tests. Maximum clique is often used as a substitute for or an approximation to maximum consensus, with empirical evidence suggesting a close relationship. However, how closely the two formulations agree is not fully understood. We study this relationship theoretically. We show that a maximum clique can have arbitrarily large alignment error and be arbitrarily larger than the maximum consensus set at any fixed positive tolerance, and derive geometric conditions that bound this error. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are sensitive to visual corruptions, but knowing that a corruption is typically harmful does not establish whether removing it would benefit the current episode. Furthermore, when several corruptions co-occur, deciding what to correct requires understanding which ones contribute to failure risk and how much their removal would help. We define this problem as failure attribution. Detecting corruption presence alone cannot answer this question, as corruptions can be present but relatively harmless, while directly measuring removal benefits requires costly paired policy rollouts with and without the corruption present. articles.title: RadGeoLoc: Radar Geolocalization via Particle Filtering
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27310v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In real-time autonomous field applications, GNSS is often unreliable and inaccurate. A possible solution is localizing against a prebuilt map like a satellite image, as it is georeferenced and already surveyed. In this work, we localize a spinning radar measurement against overhead RGB imagery with a learned observation model. We use a radar representation pretrained by masked reconstruction and align it to features from a satellite image. A particle filter propagated by radar odometry proposes candidate poses, and our observation model provides a likelihood over these poses. We evaluate our method over 31 distinct routes, over 8 datasets spanning both urban and offroad conditions using only ground radar and a coarse local prior. We also examine the robustness over changing weather using repeated traversals over the same route over 13 months, in both urban and offroad conditions.

Abstract: The integration of dynamic legged locomotion and aerial mobility offers versatility that is deterred by challenges in payload distribution, actuation, and the contrasting requirements of both domains. Abstract: Accurate head immobilization is critical for medical procedures such as neuroimaging and intracranial radiation therapy, where even minor motion can compromise precision. articles.title: Refuses When Asked, Complies When Acting: A Runtime Safety Check for Robot Control Loops
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier models can control robots through agent harnesses that loop on one question: what motion comes next toward the user's goal? We show that this default loop carries out harmful instructions. With GPT-6 Astra controlling a low-cost SO-101 arm through the Inspect Robots harness on three household tasks whose hazard is common knowledge, such as "put the knife in the toy basket", the policy refused 0% of 15 trials, attempted the harm every time, and completed it in 27%. Its one exit, give_up, is meant for goals that cannot be achieved, and it never cited the hazard. We add an optional runtime safety check to the loop: before the first motion, the model is asked whether it would carry out the instruction, given the same camera frames. The check would have stopped all 15 hazardous instructions, including the 4 that completed the harm, and flagged none of the 15 harmless controls. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27387v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Action-conditioned video generative models trained on successful, goal-directed demonstrations tend to ignore the commanded action, rendering a plausible expert-like future regardless of what is asked of them. We trace this failure to training data that lack sufficient action influence. We analyze this metric and prove that it upper bounds the action influence that any model trained on that data can express. Expert demonstrations, whose narrow action distributions let next states be predicted without attending to the action, set a low ceiling that no amount of model capacity alone can raise. Raising it requires collecting different data. We introduce Action Influence Maximization (AIM), an algorithm for actively collecting training data for improving dataset action influence. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27472v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mobile legged robots offer unique advantages for on-site construction, including the ability to traverse unstructured terrain, climb stairs, and operate independently between spatially separated work zones. This paper presents a proof-of-concept system for autonomous brick stacking using a Boston Dynamics Spot quadrupedal robot equipped with a manipulator arm. The system operates between a supply area and an assembly area, using AprilTag fiducials for localization and autowalk missions for navigation. Target brick positions and orientations are specified in CAD software and exported directly for robotic execution. We evaluate placement accuracy through ten repeated assemblies of a curved four-layer wall comprising 14 wooden bricks. articles.title: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27485v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Capability claims in robot manipulation are unverifiable, and existing leaderboards are each closed, simulated, or gameable. We propose HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark. Tasks span five skill categories at three difficulty levels and are chained so that the sensor confirming one task's completion unlocks the next, turning a room into a single long-horizon evaluation. Success is confirmed by instrumentation rather than human judgment, scoring is embodiment-agnostic, and object placements are randomized by a run-day seed. Entrants submit attested self-runs (uncut video, sensor logs, and the seed), with occasional organized events for calibration. Task specifications, build guide, bill of materials, and scoring rubrics are released under an open license.

articles.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
articles.content: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.

articles.title: AEON: Unifying Video and 3D World Models
articles.content: Current world models for explicit world simulation typically follow two distinct pathways: (1) video generative models (e.g., Sora), which simulate realistic appearances but fail to preserve 3D consistency; and (2) 3D generative models (e.g., Marble), which generate geometrically consistent scenes but often yield static, less realistic observations. We present AEON, a unified framework that bridges video-based and 3D-based world models and combines the benefits of both. The key insight of AEON lies in a generative model that operates within the text- or image-conditioned video latent space while producing renderable 4D graphics primitives---specifically, 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS)---as the explicit world representation. We train a 4D reconstruction model to predict both 4DGS and camera poses from monocular videos, serving as our initialized 4D decoder. Furthermore, we design a domain adapter that translates generative video latents into reconstructive 4D latents through a distillation process on the video VAE. AEON naturally supports video-based world modeling by rendering 4DGS at predicted camera trajectories, and constructs a persistent 4D environment with scene dynamics for realistic world simulation. Consequently, AEON empowers a diverse range of world modeling applications and achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks. Project Page: https://weiqi-zhang.github.io/AEON

articles.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
articles.content: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.

articles.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
articles.content: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.

articles.title: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
articles.content: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.

articles.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
articles.content: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).

articles.title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos
articles.content: Understanding human needs and selecting responses require distinct judgments that aggregate accuracy can obscure. We introduce PsycheMME, a video benchmark informed by psychology, with eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk. Drawing on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle, this organization separates human understanding from response selection. We construct 1,000 questions from 630 episodes through independent answering with proposed references withheld and expert review. Our Reasoning-Verified protocol weights answer credit by the support and logical consistency of explicit rationales against annotated cues. Across 17 models, Timing has the lowest Verified scores and credit retention, with weaker support judgments for correct Timing answers. Models with similar Need scores still differ in answer completeness on open questions. Input controls and SFT/GRPO examine context dependence and adaptation. Evaluating answers alongside rationales locates where models fail across understanding, response selection, and justification.

articles.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
articles.content: Warehouse robot fleets continuously observe operational conditions, but preserving these observations as reusable semantic memory incurs substantial computation, communication, and storage costs. For example, explaining recurring aisle blockages can require reviewing video from multiple robots across several shifts. We present IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand. On each robot, an NVIDIA Jetson encodes video clips into retrieval embeddings with Cosmos-Embed1, vision tokens with Cosmos3-Edge, and reconstruction latents with the Wan2.2 VAE, without uploading raw camera frames. The encoding models are re-used to detect people in image patches, zeroing them out to support PII abstraction for GDPR-compliant deployments. We split Cosmos3-Edge at its vision-language boundary, placing the vision encoder on the robot and the language decoder on an on-premises server. A Nemotron agent retrieves memories by content, position, and time and queries the decoder using cached vision tokens. This design eliminates caption generation at write time, while cached-token decoding reproduces the unsplit model's output in all 450 tested decodes.

articles.title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
articles.content: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.

articles.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
articles.content: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

articles.title: Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction: How far should we go?
articles.content: Multi-token prediction (MTP) can accelerate language-model decoding by drafting several tokens and verifying them in a single target-model pass. However, the best speculation horizon changes with context: longer drafts offer greater amortization when reliable, but can waste compute on suffixes discarded after a rejection. Unlike autoregressive drafting, where a stopping rule can decide token by token, MTP must fix the horizon before drafting, as all heads fire in the same forward pass. We therefore formulate horizon selection as an online control problem, using verification feedback to learn how far the draft can be trusted in each context, and introduce Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP): a lightweight controller that requires no retraining and leaves the exact verifier unchanged. To guide horizon selection, we characterize the expected number of tokens committed at each horizon via acceptance survival, the probability that a draft prefix is fully accepted. Before each round, AMTP predicts how far the draft is likely to survive and picks the horizon with the highest expected tokens per second, learning freely from every verification pass. Theoretically, we show that any online learner's prediction error translates into throughput regret against the best horizon for each context, and in turn into a bound on wall-clock completion time. With online gradient descent, this regret is sublinear. Across five draft-target pairings built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Medusa heads, Meta's MTP models, and Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP, evaluated on AIME 2025 and GSM8K, AMTP decodes up to 4.1x faster than standard decoding and matches or outperforms the fixed window in 8 of 10 settings, with throughput gains of up to 10%.
